reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Clear evidence of target engagement with pembrolizumab Cmax 48.9-77.8 µg/mL, dabrafenib Cmax 642-683 ng/mL, and trametinib Cmax 7.54-30.3 ng/mL achieving therapeutic levels. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: While specific pathway biomarkers aren't reported, the clinical efficacy suggests downstream biology was modulated appropriately. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Multiple primary endpoints were met - PFS improved from 9.9 to 17.0 months (HR 0.46), ORR was 65% vs 71.7% for control, and OS was 46.3 vs 26.3 months. The trial succeeded across multiple efficacy measures. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Strong biomarker-driven effects - BRAF V600 E/K mutant patients responded well to triple combination, while BRAF wild-type patients showed 50% ORR with pembrolizumab+trametinib. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Some safety concerns with dose-limiting toxicities and treatment discontinuations, but these didn't prevent efficacy demonstration.

failure_modes.evidence: Dose-limiting toxicities occurred across multiple arms with treatment discontinuations due to adverse events, though efficacy was still demonstrated
